Thanks for the detailed report and logs, Jason — they made this easy to pin down.

Your observation is correct: this is a regression introduced in 3.0.0, not an Omnirig configuration problem on your end. I traced your `wsjtx_syslog.log` through the OmniRig transceiver code.

What's happening: at startup WSJT-X writes the operating frequency to Omnirig before Omnirig has finished its first readback poll of the rig — your log shows `Mode: UNK` at that moment, meaning Omnirig knows the rig type but hasn't synced its state yet. The `QAxBase: Error calling IDispatch member FreqA` line is the result, and that's why the rig shows the frequency but won't tune. WSJT-X 2.6.1/2.7.0 deferred that first frequency write briefly, which gave Omnirig enough time; 3.0.0 dropped the deferral.

The fix is straightforward — restore the short delay before that first frequency write — and I've raised it with the team. Until a release with the fix is out, WSJT-X 2.7.0 is unaffected if you need rig control working now.

Thanks for the report, Tony. I traced the message-13 path on the current development branch and compared it against 2.7.0.

**On "introduced from v3.0":** the UDP handler for `HighlightCallsign` (message 13), the `DisplayText::highlight_callsign` code it drives, and the message schema in `NetworkMessage.hpp` are all byte-for-byte unchanged from 2.7.0 — including the `Highlight last only` handling. So this isn't a code change in that path between 2.7.0 and 3.0. It's a pre-existing behaviour, which actually helps narrow it down.

**How un-highlighting is meant to work:**

- `Highlight last only = false` → the callsign goes into a persistent set and is re-highlighted on every future decode. To **clear** it, send message 13 again for the same callsign with `Highlight last only = false` **and an invalid (default-constructed) `QColor` for both background and foreground**. That removes it from the persistent set.
- `Highlight last only = true` → only the current decode period is coloured; the callsign is **not** added to the persistent set. This mode never modifies the persistent set, so sending `true` will not clear a callsign that was previously highlighted with `false`.

If you highlighted with `false` and are trying to clear with `true`, that alone would explain "can't un-highlight" — they act on different stores.

**One genuine bug I did find:** in `highlight_callsign`, the persistent set is *populated* with the callsign upper-cased (`insert(callsign.toUpper(), …)`) but *looked up* with the callsign exactly as received (`find(callsign)`). So if your application sends a callsign in anything other than all-upper-case, the clear request silently fails to locate the entry — the callsign stays highlighted and is re-applied on the next decode. That matches your symptom.

To confirm which of these you're hitting, could you post:

1. The two message-13 packets — the one that highlights and the one meant to clear — with the callsign string, both `QColor` values, and the `Highlight last only` bool for each.
2. Whether the callsign string your application sends is all-upper-case.

If it's the case-sensitivity bug, the fix is a one-liner and I'll get it raised with the team.

DL1YCF examined the WSJT-X code and suspected that this only happens on even minutes.  All my tests were on even minutes as it happens.  Today I retested with both periods.

Tx-Even periods almost always stay in TX at timeout.
Tx-Odd periods have never resulted in TZX stuck on after many tries.   

It seems the WD timer is examined on full minute boundaries so Tx-Odd escapes the WD timer expiring just as TX is started.  The rig went to TX as commanded, and the rig returned a TX switch event which arrives in WSJT-X after the WD triggered TX->RX switch was sent.  WSJT-X then assumes the Rig chose to go to TX manually (or really, it makes no assumptions, it just follows the rig status).  

More analysis is in this thread -  https://github.com/dl1ycf/pihpsdr/issues/123

Same result with WSJT-X 3.1.0 Improved Plus.  Tx-Even with WD timeout results in Tx left on fairly often.  No audio out thus no RF out.

DL1BZ created a simple WSJTX patch with a new force_stop_tx() function for the 3.1.0_improved version that I applied and built here.  Tested against deskHPSDR, it no longer briefly switch to TX at the WD  timeout now so no longer gets stuck in TX mode.  piHPSDR did better but at least once got stuck.  Details toward the end of https://github.com/dl1ycf/pihpsdr/issues/123

The patch seems to fix the issue in WSJT-X 3.1.0 Improved at least for deskHPSDR so far, but long term testing is required sicne this can be intermittent.  I tried the patch in 3.0.2 but did not seem to help there.  

Will continue long term testing with deskHPSDR, piHPSDR and also try Thetis again with the WSJTX patch.
